cases.sentence: ___ это было так радостно, что оно казалось ему невероятным.
cases.translation: This feeling was so joyful that it seemed unbelievable to him.
cases.explain: Чувство is the subject of было, so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Он задыхался от волнения и, не в силах идти дальше, сошел с ___ в лес и сел в тени осин.
cases.translation: He was breathless with emotion and, unable to walk further, left the road for the forest and sat in the shade of the aspens.
cases.explain: The preposition с (off/from) governs the genitive case, indicating motion away from the road.

cases.sentence: Он следил за движениями зеленой букашки, поднимавшейся по ___ пырея.
cases.translation: He watched the movements of the little green bug climbing up the stalk of couch grass.
cases.explain: The preposition по (along) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Он снял с потной головы ___ и лег, облокотившись на руку, на сочную траву.
cases.translation: He took the hat off his sweaty head and lay down, leaning on his arm, on the lush grass.
cases.explain: The verb снять (to take off) governs the accusative case for its direct object.

cases.sentence: Слова, сказанные ___, произвели в его душе действие электрической искры.
cases.translation: The words spoken by the peasant produced in his soul the effect of an electric spark.
cases.explain: The instrumental case here expresses the agent, "said BY the peasant," without a preposition.

cases.sentence: Прежде я говорил, что в моем ___ совершается обмен материи, как в теле этой травы.
cases.translation: Before, I used to say that in my body an exchange of matter occurs, as in the body of this grass.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) governs the prepositional case here, denoting location.

reading.ru: Левин шел большими шагами по большой дороге, прислушиваясь не столько к своим мыслям, он не мог еще разобрать их, сколько к душевному состоянию, прежде никогда им не испытанному.
reading.question: How was Levin walking along the main road?
options: With big strides, attentive to a state of mind he had never felt before
Slowly and wearily, barely able to walk
Running as fast as he could
reading.correct: With big strides, attentive to a state of mind he had never felt before
reading.explain: The text says he walked with big strides, listening not so much to his thoughts as to a new state of mind.

reading.ru: Он чувствовал в своей душе что-то новое и с наслаждением ощупывал это новое, не зная еще, что это такое.
reading.question: What did Levin feel in his soul as he walked?
options: Something new, which he explored with delight though he didn't yet understand it
reading.correct: Something new, which he explored with delight though he didn't yet understand it
reading.explain: He felt something new in his soul and delighted in exploring it, not yet knowing what it was.

reading.ru: Не для нужд своих жить, а для Бога.
reading.question: What realization did Levin come to about how to live?
options: Not to live for one's own needs, but for God
To live entirely for his family
reading.correct: Not to live for one's own needs, but for God
reading.explain: The text states the realization: not to live for one's own needs, but for God.

reading.ru: Федор говорит, что Кириллов, дворник, живет для брюха.
reading.question: According to Levin, what does Fyodor say about the caretaker Kirillov?
options: That he lives for his belly (self-interest)
That he lives for his children
reading.correct: That he lives for his belly (self-interest)
reading.explain: Fyodor said that Kirillov, the caretaker, lives for his belly.

reading.question: How does Levin characterize the idea that people live to satisfy their own needs?
reading.explain: Levin calls the idea of living for one's belly понятно и разумно (understandable and reasonable).

reading.ru: Если добро имеет причину, оно уже не добро.
reading.question: What does Levin conclude about goodness (добро) if it has a cause?
options: Then it is no longer goodness
Then it is even greater goodness
reading.correct: Then it is no longer goodness
reading.explain: Levin reasons that if goodness has a cause, it is no longer goodness.

reading.ru: Стало быть, добро вне цепи причин и следствий.
reading.question: Where does Levin conclude that goodness (добро) exists in relation to cause and effect?
options: Outside the chain of causes and consequences
At the very center of the chain of causes
Only as a result of divine punishment
reading.correct: Outside the chain of causes and consequences
reading.explain: He concludes that goodness is outside the chain of causes and consequences.

reading.question: What had Levin previously searched for, according to this passage?
reading.explain: Levin reflects that he had been searching for miracles (чудес).

reading.ru: Чувство это было так радостно, что оно казалось ему невероятным.
reading.question: How did Levin's feeling of relief from suffering strike him?
options: It was so joyful it seemed unbelievable to him
reading.correct: It was so joyful it seemed unbelievable to him
reading.explain: The text says this feeling was so joyous that it seemed incredible to him.

reading.ru: Он задыхался от волнения и, не в силах идти дальше, сошел с дороги в лес и сел в тени осин на нескошенную траву.
reading.question: What did Levin do when he could no longer walk from emotion?
options: He left the road, went into the woods, and sat down in the shade of aspens on uncut grass
reading.correct: He left the road, went into the woods, and sat down in the shade of aspens on uncut grass
reading.explain: Breathless with emotion, he left the road for the forest and sat in the shade of aspens on unmown grass.

reading.ru: Совершается по физическим, химическим, физиологическим законам обмен материи.
reading.question: What process does Levin say occurs according to physical, chemical, and physiological laws?
reading.explain: He says an exchange of matter occurs according to physical, chemical, and physiological laws.

reading.question: What did Levin say he had freed himself from?
reading.explain: Levin declares that he freed himself from deception (обман).

reading.question: What did Levin say he had come to know?
reading.explain: Levin says he has come to know the хозяин (the master/owner, i.e., God).

reading.ru: В первый раз тогда, поняв ясно, что для всякого человека и для него впереди ничего не было, кроме страдания, смерти и вечного забвения, он решил, что так нельзя жить, что надо или объяснить свою жизнь так, чтобы она не представлялась злой насмешкой какого-то дьявола, или застрелиться.
reading.question: What had Levin decided the first time he clearly understood that suffering, death, and oblivion awaited everyone?
options: That he must either find meaning in his life or shoot himself
That he must give away all his property
reading.correct: That he must either find meaning in his life or shoot himself
reading.explain: He decided he could not live that way—he must either explain his life or shoot himself.

reading.ru: Мне сказали это в детстве, и я радостно поверил, потому что мне сказали то, что было у меня в душе.
reading.question: How does Levin say he came to believe in loving one's neighbor?
options: He was told this as a child and joyfully believed it, because it matched what was already in his soul
He deduced it through logical reasoning
He read it in a philosophy book by Spencer
Sergei Ivanovich convinced him of it
reading.correct: He was told this as a child and joyfully believed it, because it matched what was already in his soul
reading.explain: He says he was told this in childhood and joyfully believed it because it matched what was already in his soul.
